title.narrative: Emergency and Recovery Assistance to Flood Affected People of NE and SE Districts in Bangladesh 2024

description.narrative: In August 2024 many districts of north east and south east Bangladesh experienced unprecedented flooding caused by heavy rainfall over a short time period and the release of water from upstream sources. The natural mechanisms for the dispersal and evacuation of surface water have disrupted owing to the diversion or filling up of rivers and channels and the destruction or disappearance of wetlands. Floodwater inundated vast areas displacing or stranding the population and causing significant damage to property, farmland and infrastructure (roads, embankments, ponds and other structures) and cutting off essential services. Overall it was estimated that 5.82 million people were affected across 11 districts. Whilst the needs are wide ranging and cover all sectors, Caritas Bangladesh is focusing its response on 23 Upazilas in 10 districts where coverage by the Government and other agencies has been low and Caritas has a strong presence owing to existing programmes. This project will ensure that: 6,000 HHs have access to food and increased purchasing capacity for daily essential items; 3,720 HHs have access to safe drinking water, basic sanitation and hygiene kits/awareness training; 185 essential community infrastructures and 1,150 houses are repaired; and livelihood recovery assistance is provided to the most vulnerable members of the affected population.
